source_access_note: Cambridge Dictionary publisher-owned search-index snippets inspected 2026-11-02; direct Cambridge headword page opens returned HTTP 403. Indexed labels are leads only, not independently verified direct publisher-page CEFR observations. No human-independent linguistic review, real listening, iPhone test or deployment was performed.

original.english_definition: Expected or arranged to happen at a particular time.
original.burmese_meaning: သတ်မှတ်ချိန်တွင် ဖြစ်ရန်ရှိသော
original.example_sentence: The next bus is due in ten minutes.

publisher_evidence.indexed_exact_sense: due adjective (EXPECTED): expected to happen or arrive at a particular time; Cambridge-indexed B1
publisher_evidence.other_sense_warning: Do not confuse expected arrival with due to (because), money owed (C2), or in due course (B2).

entries.editorial_finding: Frozen A2 adjective and bus-arrival example match the indexed B1 EXPECTED sense, not the other due senses.

original.example_sentence: The new instructions are pretty clear.

publisher_evidence.indexed_exact_sense: pretty adverb (DEGREE): quite, but not extremely; Cambridge-indexed B1
publisher_evidence.other_sense_warning: The A2 Cambridge label belongs to the adjective meaning attractive, not the frozen informal adverb.

entries.editorial_finding: Frozen A2 adverb fairly/not extremely and example pretty clear align with indexed B1 adverb; adjective pretty has a separate A2 badge.

original.english_definition: An idea or opinion that comes into your mind.
original.example_sentence: One thought kept me awake last night.

publisher_evidence.indexed_exact_sense: thought noun (IDEA): an idea or opinion; Cambridge-indexed B1
publisher_evidence.other_sense_warning: Do not use the past-tense verb thought as evidence for the noun; careful thinking is a separate B2 learner-dictionary sense.

entries.editorial_finding: Frozen A2 countable idea/opinion noun and One thought example match the Cambridge-indexed B1 noun, not the verb form.

unapproved_teaching_alternative.example_sentence: A strange thought came into her mind.

original.english_definition: To touch something suddenly and with force.
original.burmese_meaning: ပြင်းပြင်းထန်ထန် ထိမိသည်၊ ရိုက်မိသည်
original.example_sentence: The ball hit the window during the game.

publisher_evidence.indexed_exact_sense: hit verb (TOUCH): A2 striking with hand or hand-held object; B1 sudden-force collision of a moving object
publisher_evidence.other_sense_warning: Cambridge Essential British English gives a broader A2 gloss including a ball hitting someone; the Advanced Learner's Dictionary separates A2 hand/object strike from B1 collision. Publisher/dictionary edition distinction requires independent adjudication.

entries.editorial_finding: Frozen definition is broad and ball-hit-window example is a moving-object collision, aligned more closely with Cambridge Advanced Learner's B1 collision than its A2 hand-striking example; Essential British A2 is a competing publisher lead.

unapproved_teaching_alternative.english_definition: To strike someone or something with your hand or an object you are holding.
unapproved_teaching_alternative.burmese_meaning: လက်ဖြင့် သို့မဟုတ် လက်ထဲတွင် ကိုင်ထားသော ပစ္စည်းတစ်ခုဖြင့် တစ်စုံတစ်ဦး သို့မဟုတ် တစ်စုံတစ်ခုကို ရိုက်သည်။
unapproved_teaching_alternative.example_sentence: She hit the ball with a tennis racket.

original.english_definition: A message or item shared on a website or social platform.
original.burmese_meaning: အွန်လိုင်းတွင် တင်ထားသော စာ သို့မဟုတ် အကြောင်းအရာ
original.example_sentence: Her post explained the new class schedule.

publisher_evidence.indexed_exact_sense: post noun (MESSAGE): a message or picture published on a website or social media; no CEFR badge observed in Cambridge-indexed noun section
publisher_evidence.other_sense_warning: Cambridge B1 label applies to the separate internet/social-media verb post, not automatically to the frozen noun; also distinguish British postal noun.

entries.editorial_finding: Frozen A2 noun and class-schedule example match the unlabelled Cambridge internet-message noun; B1 internet verb is not valid exact-POS evidence for A2 noun.

unapproved_teaching_alternative.english_definition: A message, picture or other item published on a website or social media.
unapproved_teaching_alternative.burmese_meaning: ဝက်ဘ်ဆိုက် သို့မဟုတ် လူမှုကွန်ရက်ပေါ်တွင် တင်ထားသော စာသား၊ ဓာတ်ပုံ သို့မဟုတ် အခြားအကြောင်းအရာတစ်ခု။
unapproved_teaching_alternative.example_sentence: Her post included the timetable for the new class.
